assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
a dense upstream machine_summary supplies the facts every prompt field is grounded in
the downstream agent session shares no state with this one; the boundary is stateless
this stage produces prompts only and never renders, synthesizes, or publishes media
exclusions: image/story/audio synthesis and rendering (the downstream session's job)
generation of the upstream machine_summary itself
the legal drafting of disclosure-law text (only its carriage in-band is in scope)
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for downstream prompt-brief compilation work units, informed by creative-brief practice, prompt-engineering pattern catalogs, latent-diffusion text conditioning, separation of concerns, and design-by-contract; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Rombach et al. 2022 High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models (text conditioning, classifier-free guidance, negative prompts); White et al. 2023 A Prompt Pattern Catalog to Enhance Prompt Engineering with ChatGPT; Dijkstra 1982 On the Role of Scientific Thought (separation of concerns); Meyer 1992 Applying Design by Contract (assume/guarantee); creative-brief practice (objective/audience/deliverable/constraints)

competency_questions.question: What fixed, versioned schema does the emitted prompt-brief artifact take, and which blocks are required versus optional?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROMPT_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA defines the versioned block set with image/story required and audio optional

competency_questions.question: How is every prompt field grounded in the dense upstream machine_summary rather than invented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GROUND_FROM_SUMMARY maps each field to a named summary fact under a no-invention rule

competency_questions.question: How is the image-prompt block structured for text-to-image conditioning, including negative constraints?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IMAGE_PROMPT_SPEC defines subject/style/composition/lighting plus a negative-constraint list

competency_questions.question: How is the story/script-prompt block structured to control premise, beats, voice, and length?
How is the optional audio-brief specified so synthesis is non-impersonating by default unless consent is referenced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIO_BRIEF_SPEC defines script + abstract voice description + non-impersonation default + consent slot

competency_questions.question: How does the safety/disclosure contract travel in-band so a stateless downstream session cannot miss it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IN_BAND_CONTRACT embeds disclosure tokens and assume/guarantee clauses in the payload, closing the SPOF

competency_questions.question: How is the mandatory synthetic-media disclosure label guaranteed to be present in the artifact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCLOSURE_SLOT enforces a non-empty label-and-placement slot

competency_questions.question: How is scope contained so this stage produces prompts and never renders or publishes?
How is the artifact emitted now and made safe to inject into a separate stateless downstream session later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF serializes a self-contained artifact for a stateless boundary

competency_questions.question: How is the brief made reproducible and traceable to the facts and contract clauses it drew on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DETERMINISM_PROVENANCE records a field-to-source map and a deterministic build

competency_questions.question: How is downstream parseability and contract presence validated before the artifact is emitted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HANDOFF_VALIDATION schema-validates blocks and checks disclosure/contract presence

competency_questions.question: Why must the disclosure/safety contract travel in-band, and what is the single point of failure if it does not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IN_BAND_CONTRACT and DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF show that an out-of-band contract is dropped at the stateless boundary (the SPOF)

competency_questions.question: How are prompts shaped to the downstream model's actual capabilities and framed with role, constraint, brief-objective, and a negotiated schema version?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TARGET_MODEL_PROFILE, ROLE_FRAMING, BRIEF_OBJECTIVE_FRAME, and SCHEMA_VERSION_PIN shape prompts to the consumer

competency_questions.question: How are safety exclusions, consent for real-person likeness/voice, deterministic serialization, consumer attestation, and emission audit handled across the brief?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEGATIVE_CONSTRAINT_SET, CONSENT_REFERENCE, ARTIFACT_SERIALIZATION, CONTRACT_ATTESTATION, and EMISSION_AUDIT_LOG cover safety, consent, serialization, attestation, and audit

glossary.definition: the structured, versioned object this stage emits, bundling image/story/optional-audio prompt blocks with a disclosure and in-band contract header
the safety/disclosure/usage clauses carried inside the artifact payload so a stateless consumer receives them with the prompt
an explicit list of content the downstream image model must avoid, mapped onto diffusion negative prompting
a mandatory non-empty artifact field naming the synthetic-media label and where it must appear
a session boundary across which no prior context is shared, so the artifact must be fully self-contained
the discipline of producing prompts only and delegating rendering/publishing downstream, containing this stage's scope
a design-by-contract pair stating what the producer guarantees and what the consumer must assume, carried in-band
the audio-brief default that voice is steered by abstract description rather than a named real person absent a consent reference
a reference from a prompt field to the machine_summary fact or contract clause that produced it

nodes.definition: Define the closed schema of the emitted prompt-brief artifact: a structured image-prompt block, a story/script-prompt block, and an OPTIONAL audio-brief block, plus a header carrying the disclosure and in-band contract slots, so every consumer parses one fixed, versioned shape.

base.update_signal: artifact schema version or required-block set changes

pros.claim: A single versioned artifact schema makes the brief machine-parseable and lets the downstream session validate before acting
pros.example: header.schema_version=1 with image/story blocks required and audio optional

cons.claim: A rigid schema can lag a new media type and force out-of-band side channels until it is extended
cons.example: a new 3D-asset prompt has no block and gets smuggled into the story field

failure_modes: under-specified blocks force guessing downstream
optional audio block silently treated as required
acceptance_tests: the artifact validates against its declared schema_version and every required block is present and typed
revisit_triggers: a new downstream media type is requested
schema version bumped

nodes.definition: Construct every prompt-brief field strictly from the dense upstream machine_summary fields (subject, entities, claims, constraints), never from free invention, so the brief is traceable to source facts rather than hallucinated detail.

base.update_signal: machine_summary field schema or grounding policy changes

pros.claim: Grounding each prompt field in a named summary fact makes the brief auditable and curbs hallucinated subjects
pros.example: image subject pulled from summary.primary_entity, not invented

cons.claim: Strict grounding can starve a prompt of the connotative detail that makes generations vivid
cons.example: a summary lists 'a city' but no mood, yielding a flat image prompt

failure_modes: prompt invents a subject absent from the summary
summary field misread into the wrong block
acceptance_tests: every populated prompt field cites at least one machine_summary field as its source
revisit_triggers: machine_summary schema changes
an ungrounded invented detail is found in a brief

nodes.definition: Specify the image-prompt block as structured fields -- subject, style, composition/framing, lighting, and an explicit negative-constraint list -- aligned to text-to-image conditioning so a downstream diffusion model can be steered without prose ambiguity.

base.update_signal: downstream image-model conditioning interface changes

pros.claim: Structured fields plus a negative list map directly onto diffusion text-conditioning and classifier-free guidance, steering output and suppressing unwanted content
pros.example: negative: 'text, watermark, extra fingers' removes common diffusion artifacts (Rombach et al. 2022)

cons.claim: Over-stuffed prompts dilute the conditioning signal and can fight classifier-free guidance, degrading coherence
cons.example: fifteen competing style tokens yield a muddy, averaged image

failure_modes: negative list omitted, so disallowed content reappears
style and subject fields contradict each other
acceptance_tests: the image block contains a non-empty subject and a negative-constraint list and validates against the schema
revisit_triggers: downstream image model or its prompt syntax changes
generations repeatedly violate a negative constraint

nodes.definition: Specify the story/script-prompt block as structured fields -- premise, beat outline, narrative voice/POV, tone, and target length -- so a downstream text model produces a story or script with controlled structure rather than an open-ended ramble.

base.update_signal: story prompt field set or length-control policy changes

pros.claim: Beat-outlined, length-bounded prompts give the downstream model a scaffold, improving coherence and controllability over a single instruction
pros.example: five-beat outline plus 'second person, present tense, 300 words' yields a structured micro-story

cons.claim: Heavy structural constraints can suppress the model's narrative creativity and produce formulaic output
cons.example: rigid beats force a predictable arc and flatten voice

failure_modes: length target absent, output runs unbounded
voice/POV unspecified, tone drifts mid-story
acceptance_tests: the story block declares a premise, a beat outline, and a target length and validates against the schema
revisit_triggers: downstream text model changes
stories repeatedly miss the target length or voice

nodes.definition: Specify the OPTIONAL audio-brief block -- script text, an abstract voice DESCRIPTION (timbre/pace/register), and a default NON-impersonating constraint with a consent-reference slot -- so any downstream TTS or voice synthesis is steered by description, never by an identifiable real person, unless explicit consent is referenced in-band.

base.update_signal: voice-cloning policy, consent model, or audio synthesis interface changes

pros.claim: Describing a voice abstractly and defaulting to non-impersonation lets audio be steered without cloning a real person's identity
pros.example: voice: 'warm mid-range female narrator, unhurried' instead of naming a celebrity

cons.claim: Abstract voice description gives less precise control than a reference clip, so timbre may vary run to run
cons.example: 'gravelly older male' admits a wide range of realized voices

failure_modes: a named real person is requested without a consent reference
consent slot left empty but impersonation implied
acceptance_tests: if present, the audio block carries a script, an abstract voice description, and either a non-impersonation default or a populated consent reference
revisit_triggers: voice-cloning or consent policy changes
an impersonation request appears without consent

nodes.definition: Carry the safety/disclosure contract -- required synthetic-media disclosure tokens, usage restrictions, and the assume/guarantee clauses -- IN-BAND inside the artifact payload, so the downstream session (which shares no state with this one) receives the contract WITH the prompt instead of assuming it by reference. This closes the single point of failure where an out-of-band contract is silently dropped at the session boundary.

base.update_signal: disclosure law, safety policy, or the assume/guarantee contract clauses change

excluded: legal drafting of the policy text itself

pros.claim: Embedding the contract in the payload makes the safety assumption a guaranteed precondition delivered to the consumer, not a fragile cross-session assumption (Meyer design-by-contract; in-band signalling closes the SPOF)
pros.example: the brief itself states 'mark output as AI-generated' so a stateless downstream session cannot miss it

cons.claim: In-band contract text adds payload weight and can be stripped or ignored by a non-compliant consumer if not validated
cons.example: a downstream tool truncates the header and loses the disclosure clause

failure_modes: contract assumed downstream by reference and never delivered (the SPOF)
in-band clause present but unvalidated and silently ignored
acceptance_tests: the artifact payload contains the disclosure tokens, usage restrictions, and assume/guarantee clauses with a contract version, verifiable without any external lookup
revisit_triggers: disclosure regulation or safety policy changes
a downstream session is found acting without the contract

nodes.definition: Provide a mandatory, non-empty disclosure slot in the artifact that names the required synthetic-media label and where it must appear, so downstream generation always carries an AI-generated/synthetic-content label as a hard precondition of the contract.

base.update_signal: synthetic-media labeling requirements or placement rules change

excluded: the legal text of disclosure law

pros.claim: A mandatory non-empty slot makes the synthetic-media label a structural requirement that cannot be forgotten downstream
pros.example: slot: label='AI-generated', placement='visible caption + metadata'

cons.claim: A single generic label may not satisfy every jurisdiction's specific disclosure wording
cons.example: one region requires a longer prescribed sentence the generic label omits

failure_modes: disclosure slot left empty yet artifact still validates
label specified but no placement, so it is rendered invisibly
acceptance_tests: the disclosure slot is non-empty, names a label and a placement, and the schema rejects an empty slot
revisit_triggers: labeling regulation changes
an unlabeled synthetic output is produced downstream

nodes.definition: Enforce that this stage PRODUCES prompt-briefs only and NEVER renders, synthesizes, or publishes media -- a strict separation of concerns (Dijkstra) that contains scope, so generation and distribution are the downstream session's responsibility under the carried contract.

base.update_signal: stage responsibility boundary or pipeline ownership changes

pros.claim: Separating prompt production from rendering contains this stage's scope and blast radius: a bug here cannot publish unsafe media, only emit a brief (Dijkstra separation of concerns)
pros.example: this stage has no render or post capability wired in at all

cons.claim: A hard boundary adds a handoff step and latency versus an end-to-end pipeline that generates inline
cons.example: two sessions and a serialization round-trip instead of one call

failure_modes: this stage gains a render/publish path, collapsing the separation
scope creep adds distribution responsibilities here
acceptance_tests: this stage exposes no render or publish capability; its only output is a prompt-brief artifact
revisit_triggers: pipeline ownership boundaries change
a render or publish path appears in this stage

nodes.definition: Emit the prompt-brief now for injection into a SEPARATE downstream agent session later; treat the handoff as a stateless boundary where nothing from this session's context is available unless it was serialized into the artifact.

base.update_signal: handoff transport, serialization format, or session boundary semantics change

included: no reliance on this session's context

pros.claim: Treating the boundary as stateless forces everything the consumer needs -- including the contract -- into the artifact, eliminating dropped-context failures
pros.example: the brief carries subject, style, AND disclosure so a fresh session needs no back-reference

cons.claim: A fully self-contained artifact duplicates context and is larger than a referenced handoff
cons.example: the disclosure and source facts are restated rather than linked

failure_modes: handoff relies on shared state that the new session lacks
artifact references an id the downstream session cannot resolve
acceptance_tests: the emitted artifact is self-contained: a fresh session with no prior context can act on it using only the payload
revisit_triggers: handoff transport or serialization format changes
a downstream session fails for lack of carried context

nodes.definition: Record the provenance of the brief: which machine_summary fields and which contract/disclosure clauses each prompt field drew on, so the same inputs reproduce the same brief and any field is traceable back to its source fact.

base.update_signal: provenance schema or determinism requirement changes

pros.claim: A provenance map makes the brief reproducible and auditable: every field points at the summary fact or contract clause that produced it
pros.example: image.subject -> summary.entity[0]; header.disclosure -> contract.clause[2]

cons.claim: Provenance records add weight and must be kept in sync when a field is edited
cons.example: an edited style field whose provenance pointer was not updated misleads an auditor

failure_modes: provenance pointer stale after a field edit
a field has no recorded source, blocking audit
acceptance_tests: every prompt field carries a provenance pointer to a summary field or contract clause and rebuilds deterministically from them
revisit_triggers: provenance schema changes
a non-reproducible brief is observed for identical inputs

nodes.definition: Validate, before emission, that a downstream consumer can parse the artifact: schema-validate every block, confirm the disclosure slot and in-band contract are present and non-empty, and confirm no required field is missing, so a malformed brief is caught here rather than failing in the separate session.

base.update_signal: validation contract or downstream parser expectations change

included: presence/non-empty checks for disclosure and contract

pros.claim: Validating parseability and contract presence at emission time turns a downstream parse failure into a local, fixable error and guarantees the safety contract ships
pros.example: validator rejects a brief whose disclosure slot is empty before it ever leaves this stage

cons.claim: Validation only checks structure, not whether a permissive downstream consumer will honor the carried contract
cons.example: a consumer parses the brief yet ignores the disclosure clause

failure_modes: validator passes a brief missing the in-band contract
downstream parser is stricter than the validator, so a valid-here brief still fails there
acceptance_tests: the validator rejects any artifact with a missing block, an empty disclosure slot, or an absent in-band contract before emission
revisit_triggers: downstream parser contract changes
a brief that passed validation fails to parse downstream

nodes.definition: Declare the downstream model/agent profile each block targets -- modality, prompt syntax dialect, token budget, and supported controls (e.g. negative prompts, system role) -- so block fields are shaped to controls the consumer actually honors rather than to a generic ideal.

base.update_signal: downstream model roster or its supported-control set changes

pros.claim: Profiling the target lets the brief use controls the consumer honors (negative prompts, system role) instead of tokens it ignores
pros.example: skip a negative-prompt field for a model with no classifier-free guidance

cons.claim: Profiles drift as vendors change syntax, so a stale profile shapes prompts for controls that no longer exist
cons.example: a model deprecates a weighting syntax the profile still emits

failure_modes: block shaped to a control the target does not support
token budget exceeds the target's context window
acceptance_tests: each block declares the target profile it was shaped for
revisit_triggers: the downstream model roster changes
a supported-control assumption is found stale

nodes.definition: Apply role/constraint prompt-engineering patterns to each block: set the downstream model's role, state hard constraints as imperatives, and order constraints before content, so the brief steers behavior through pattern rather than hope.

base.update_signal: prompt-pattern catalog or role-framing convention changes

pros.claim: Role and constraint patterns are documented to improve controllability and reduce drift versus a bare instruction (White et al. 2023 prompt pattern catalog)
pros.example: 'You are a storyboard artist. Hard constraints: ... Now render the scene as:'

cons.claim: Over-engineered role framing can crowd out the actual content and waste the token budget
cons.example: a long persona preamble leaves little budget for the subject

failure_modes: constraints buried after content and ignored
role framing contradicts the carried contract
acceptance_tests: each block applies a role and states its hard constraints as imperatives before content
revisit_triggers: prompt-pattern conventions change
role framing is found to crowd out content

nodes.definition: Frame each block with the creative-brief essentials -- objective, audience, deliverable, and constraints -- so the downstream generation has the same orienting context a human creative brief provides, not just raw fields.

base.update_signal: creative-brief field conventions change

pros.claim: Carrying objective/audience/deliverable/constraints gives the downstream model the orienting frame a human creative brief provides, improving on-target output
pros.example: objective: 'evoke calm'; audience: 'wellness app users'; deliverable: 'square hero image'

cons.claim: A full brief frame adds length and can over-specify when a single field would suffice
cons.example: a one-word subject wrapped in a paragraph of brief boilerplate

failure_modes: objective missing, so output is technically correct but off-purpose
audience omitted, tone misjudged
acceptance_tests: each block states an objective, an audience, and a deliverable definition
revisit_triggers: creative-brief conventions change
outputs are on-spec but off-objective

nodes.definition: Compile the consolidated negative/safety constraint set spanning all blocks -- disallowed visual content, prohibited narrative themes, and audio exclusions -- and map it onto each modality's exclusion mechanism, so safety exclusions are uniform rather than per-block afterthoughts.

base.update_signal: prohibited-content policy or per-modality exclusion mechanism changes

pros.claim: A single consolidated exclusion set mapped per modality keeps safety constraints uniform across image, story, and audio instead of per-block afterthoughts
pros.example: one 'no real minors' rule mapped to image negatives, story themes, and audio script

cons.claim: A blanket exclusion set can be over-broad and suppress legitimate content in one modality to satisfy another
cons.example: an image-motivated exclusion needlessly blocks a benign story theme

failure_modes: an exclusion applied to one block but missed in another
exclusion set diverges from the carried contract
acceptance_tests: the same disallowed-content set is mapped onto every block's exclusion mechanism
revisit_triggers: prohibited-content policy changes
an exclusion is found missing in one modality

nodes.definition: Specify the consent-reference mechanism for any depiction or voice of an identifiable real person: a structured reference to a consent record carried in-band, defaulting to absent (which forces non-impersonation/non-likeness), so identity use is gated on explicit, traceable consent.

base.update_signal: consent model, likeness law, or reference format changes

pros.claim: A default-absent, in-band consent reference makes real-person likeness and voice use traceable and gated, not implicit
pros.example: consent_ref empty => image must not depict a recognizable real person; populated => allowed and logged

cons.claim: A reference cannot verify the consent record's validity, only assert it exists, so a forged reference still passes structurally
cons.example: a consent_ref points to a record that does not actually grant the use

failure_modes: likeness used with an empty consent reference
consent reference present but pointing to an invalid record
acceptance_tests: any real-person likeness or voice carries a populated, in-band consent reference; otherwise it is gated off
revisit_triggers: consent or likeness policy changes
a likeness is used without a valid consent reference

nodes.definition: Serialize the assembled brief into a canonical, deterministic on-the-wire form (stable field order, explicit encoding, schema_version header) so the same logical brief always serializes identically and the downstream parser has an unambiguous input.

base.update_signal: serialization format or canonicalization rules change

included: schema_version header in the wire form

pros.claim: Canonical, deterministic serialization gives a stable wire form so identical briefs are byte-identical and the parser input is unambiguous
pros.example: stable key order plus UTF-8 makes two builds of the same brief diff-clean

cons.claim: Canonicalization constrains the wire form and can complicate streaming or partial emission
cons.example: a strict canonical order blocks emitting blocks as they are ready

failure_modes: non-deterministic field order breaks byte-level reproducibility
encoding left implicit, parsed wrongly downstream
acceptance_tests: the same logical brief serializes to an identical canonical wire form on every build
revisit_triggers: serialization format changes
a non-deterministic serialization is observed

nodes.definition: Pin and negotiate the artifact schema_version against the downstream parser's supported range, so producer and consumer agree on the shape before emission and a version mismatch is caught here rather than as a silent misparse downstream.

base.update_signal: schema versioning policy or downstream supported-range changes

pros.claim: Negotiating the schema version against the consumer's supported range catches a shape mismatch at emission instead of as a silent downstream misparse
pros.example: producer emits v2 only if the consumer advertises support for v2

cons.claim: Strict version negotiation can block a brief when a consumer lags behind a new schema version
cons.example: a consumer stuck on v1 cannot receive a v2-only block

failure_modes: version mismatch silently misparsed downstream
producer emits a version the consumer cannot read
acceptance_tests: the pinned schema_version lies within the downstream parser's supported range before emission
revisit_triggers: schema versioning policy changes
a version mismatch reaches the downstream parser

nodes.definition: Require the downstream consumer to attest, as its own precondition, that it has parsed and will honor the in-band contract (apply the disclosure label, respect usage restrictions) before it generates, turning structural contract presence into a behavioral guarantee at the consumer boundary.

base.update_signal: consumer attestation protocol or contract honoring requirements change

pros.claim: Requiring an attestation makes the carried contract a behavioral precondition of generation, not merely structurally present text the consumer may ignore (Meyer design-by-contract: the consumer's assume becomes its obligation)
pros.example: consumer must echo 'disclosure applied' before any pixels are produced

cons.claim: This stage can require attestation but cannot enforce it inside a non-cooperative consumer, so a malicious consumer can still lie
cons.example: a rogue downstream tool attests then drops the label

failure_modes: consumer parses the contract but never attests, generating anyway
attestation faked by a non-compliant consumer
acceptance_tests: the brief requires a consumer attestation of contract compliance as a precondition of downstream generation
revisit_triggers: attestation protocol changes
a consumer generates without attesting

nodes.definition: Write an emission audit log: for each emitted brief, record its schema_version, contract version, disclosure directive, provenance map digest, and target profile, so emissions are auditable and a brief can be reconstructed or recalled if a policy later changes.

base.update_signal: audit-log schema or retention/recall policy changes

pros.claim: An emission audit log makes every brief reconstructable and recallable, so a later policy change can identify and reissue affected briefs
pros.example: a disclosure-law update finds all emissions with the old directive via the log

cons.claim: Audit logging adds storage and a retention obligation, and the log itself must be access-controlled
cons.example: logged contract text and provenance become sensitive records to protect

failure_modes: emission not logged, so an affected brief cannot be found after a policy change
log records a digest that does not match the emitted artifact
acceptance_tests: every emitted brief writes an audit record capturing its schema/contract/disclosure versions and provenance digest
revisit_triggers: audit-log or recall policy changes
an emission is found with no audit record

edges.why_related: the disclosure slot must be serialized into the handoff artifact or the contract is lost at the boundary
carrying the contract in-band is what lets this stage refuse to render yet still bind the downstream consumer
synthetic audio inherits the same mandatory disclosure obligation as image and story output
image and story blocks share the structured-field pattern and must stay mutually consistent on subject and tone
validation failures that recur drive a schema revision to make the missing field structurally required
because this stage does not render, the handoff is the mechanism by which generation happens at all
the required consumer attestation is checked for presence as part of pre-emission validation

edges.resolution_rule: always serialize the full contract into the artifact even though it enlarges the payload: a self-contained, larger handoff is mandatory over a smaller one that references an out-of-band contract the stateless session cannot fetch
edges.why_related: minimizing handoff payload size conflicts with carrying the entire safety/disclosure contract in-band
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the brief or its safety guarantee

edges.resolution_rule: ground all factual fields (subject, named entities) strictly in the summary, but allow stylistic fields (style, lighting, mood) to add connotative detail not in the summary, marking them as non-factual embellishment in provenance
edges.why_related: strict summary-grounding conflicts with the evocative detail that makes an image prompt vivid
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the brief or its safety guarantee

edges.resolution_rule: keep render/publish strictly downstream; accept the extra handoff latency and serialization round-trip as the price of scope containment rather than collapsing the stages into one inline pipeline
edges.why_related: a strict no-render boundary conflicts with the lower latency of an end-to-end inline pipeline
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the brief or its safety guarantee

edges.resolution_rule: default audio to non-impersonating abstract description AND require the disclosure label; when a consent reference is supplied it relaxes impersonation but never the disclosure obligation
edges.why_related: precise voice control via a named reference conflicts with the non-impersonation default and the mandatory disclosure obligation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the brief or its safety guarantee

conflict_axes.name: in_band_contract_vs_payload_size
conflict_axes.description: Carrying the full safety/disclosure contract in the payload guarantees a stateless consumer receives it, but enlarges the handoff versus an out-of-band reference.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always carry the contract in-band; size is the accepted cost of closing the SPOF

conflict_axes.name: summary_grounding_vs_evocative_detail
conflict_axes.description: Strictly grounding fields in the machine_summary keeps the brief auditable but can starve prompts of vivid connotative detail.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ground factual fields strictly; allow marked stylistic embellishment in provenance

conflict_axes.name: scope_containment_vs_inline_pipeline
conflict_axes.description: Producing prompts only contains scope and blast radius but adds a handoff versus an end-to-end inline generator.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the no-render boundary; accept handoff latency as the price of containment

conflict_axes.name: non_impersonation_default_vs_voice_fidelity
conflict_axes.description: Defaulting audio to abstract non-impersonating description protects identity but yields less precise voice control than a named reference.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: abstract description by default; relax only with an in-band consent reference, never the disclosure

conflict_axes.name: schema_rigidity_vs_media_extensibility
conflict_axes.description: A closed versioned schema makes the brief reliably parseable but lags new media types until it is extended.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: version the schema and extend deliberately; forbid out-of-band side channels

conflict_axes.name: self_contained_artifact_vs_context_duplication
conflict_axes.description: A self-contained handoff eliminates dropped-context failures but duplicates context the upstream already holds.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: serialize everything the consumer needs; duplication is cheaper than a dropped contract

conflict_axes.name: prompt_specificity_vs_conditioning_dilution
conflict_axes.description: More structured prompt tokens steer generation precisely but, over-stuffed, dilute the conditioning signal and degrade coherence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer a few high-signal fields plus a negative list over many competing tokens

conflict_axes.name: validation_strictness_vs_emission_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Strict pre-emission validation guarantees a parseable, contract-bearing artifact but rejects more briefs and slows emission.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hard-fail only on missing blocks, empty disclosure, or absent contract; warn on the rest

conflict_axes.name: structural_presence_vs_downstream_compliance
conflict_axes.description: Validating that the contract is structurally present does not guarantee a permissive downstream consumer will honor it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: guarantee presence here; require the consumer to attest compliance as its own precondition

edge_cases.description: The disclosure/safety contract is assumed to be known downstream and is left out of the artifact; the stateless session never receives it and generates unlabeled synthetic media.
edge_cases.trigger: contract carried out-of-band by reference instead of in-band (the single point of failure)
edge_cases.mitigation: embed the full contract and disclosure tokens in the payload; validation hard-fails an artifact lacking them

edge_cases.description: The disclosure slot is left empty yet the artifact still passes as valid, so downstream output carries no synthetic-media label.
edge_cases.trigger: schema does not enforce a non-empty disclosure slot
edge_cases.mitigation: make the slot a required non-empty field with a placement directive; reject empty slots at validation

edge_cases.description: This stage acquires a render or publish path and generates media inline, collapsing the separation of concerns and widening the blast radius.
edge_cases.trigger: scope creep wires a generation/publish capability into the prompt stage
edge_cases.mitigation: assert no render/publish capability is wired in; the only output is a prompt-brief artifact

edge_cases.description: An audio brief requests a named real person's voice with no consent reference, inviting impersonation.
edge_cases.trigger: named-voice request without a populated consent slot
edge_cases.mitigation: default to abstract non-impersonating description; require an in-band consent reference to name a real person

edge_cases.description: A prompt field invents a subject or entity absent from the machine_summary, producing a brief untraceable to source facts.
edge_cases.trigger: grounding rule not enforced; free invention permitted
edge_cases.mitigation: require each factual field to cite a summary fact; mark stylistic embellishment separately in provenance

edge_cases.description: The handoff relies on this session's context (an id or memory) that the fresh downstream session cannot resolve, so the brief fails when injected.
edge_cases.trigger: artifact references shared state instead of being self-contained
edge_cases.mitigation: serialize everything the consumer needs into the payload; validation rejects unresolved references

edge_cases.description: The image block omits the negative-constraint list, so disallowed content (watermarks, text, artifacts) reappears in generations.
edge_cases.trigger: negative list treated as optional and left empty
edge_cases.mitigation: require a non-empty negative-constraint list in the image block schema

edge_cases.description: An over-stuffed image prompt with many competing style tokens dilutes conditioning and yields an incoherent, averaged image.
edge_cases.trigger: too many low-signal tokens crammed into the prompt
edge_cases.mitigation: favor a few high-signal fields plus a negative list; cap competing style tokens

edge_cases.description: A provenance pointer goes stale after a field is edited, so an auditor is misled about a field's source.
edge_cases.trigger: field edited without updating its provenance pointer
edge_cases.mitigation: rebuild provenance on every field edit; validation flags fields without a current source pointer

edge_cases.description: The story prompt omits a length target, so the downstream model produces unbounded output that overruns its budget.
edge_cases.trigger: length field left unset in the story block
edge_cases.mitigation: require a target length and structural bounds in the story block schema

edge_cases.description: The artifact passes this stage's validator but the downstream parser is stricter, so a brief valid here still fails there.
edge_cases.trigger: downstream parser contract diverges from this stage's validation contract
edge_cases.mitigation: pin the validator to the downstream parser contract and version them together

edge_cases.description: The contract is present in-band but the downstream consumer parses the brief and then ignores the disclosure clause.
edge_cases.trigger: structural presence guaranteed but behavioral compliance not required of the consumer
edge_cases.mitigation: require the consumer to attest contract compliance as its own precondition before generating

workflow.description: Pin the versioned artifact schema: header plus image/story required blocks and an optional audio block.
workflow.gate: schema_version set and required/optional blocks declared

workflow.description: Map each factual prompt field to a named machine_summary fact under a no-invention rule.
workflow.gate: every factual field cites a summary fact

workflow.description: Populate subject/style/composition/lighting and a non-empty negative-constraint list.
workflow.gate: subject present and negative list non-empty

workflow.description: Populate premise, beat outline, voice/POV, tone, and a target length.
If audio is requested, populate script and an abstract voice description with a non-impersonation default or a consent reference.
workflow.gate: non-impersonation default or populated consent reference present

workflow.description: Embed disclosure tokens, usage restrictions, and assume/guarantee clauses with a contract version into the payload.
workflow.gate: contract clauses and version present in payload

workflow.description: Populate the mandatory synthetic-media label and its placement directive.
workflow.gate: disclosure slot non-empty with label and placement

workflow.description: Assert this stage exposes no render or publish capability; output is the brief only.
Record the field-to-source map and a deterministic build record for reproducibility.
workflow.gate: every field has a current source pointer

workflow.description: Serialize a self-contained artifact for injection into a separate stateless downstream session.
workflow.gate: artifact is self-contained with no unresolved references

workflow.description: Schema-validate all blocks and confirm disclosure and in-band contract are present and non-empty.
workflow.gate: no missing block, empty disclosure, or absent contract

workflow.description: Emit the validated prompt-brief artifact for downstream injection; this stage does not render or publish.
workflow.gate: validated artifact emitted; no media rendered here

dominance_rules.rule: The in-band contract and disclosure tokens must be embedded in the payload before DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF emits the artifact
dominance_rules.rationale: a stateless downstream session that never receives the contract is the single point of failure; an out-of-band contract is silently dropped
dominance_rules.trigger: emission attempted without the contract embedded
dominance_rules.action: block emission until the contract and disclosure tokens are in the payload

dominance_rules.rule: The disclosure slot must be non-empty before HANDOFF_VALIDATION passes
dominance_rules.rationale: an empty disclosure slot yields unlabeled synthetic media downstream
dominance_rules.trigger: validation run on an artifact with an empty disclosure slot
dominance_rules.action: fail validation and route back to DISCLOSURE_SLOT

dominance_rules.rule: SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS must hold: no render or publish capability may exist in this stage
dominance_rules.rationale: scope containment keeps a bug here from publishing unsafe media
dominance_rules.trigger: a render or publish path is detected in the stage
dominance_rules.action: remove the path and re-assert the no-render boundary

dominance_rules.rule: Factual prompt fields must be grounded in the machine_summary before IMAGE_PROMPT_SPEC or STORY_PROMPT_SPEC finalize
dominance_rules.rationale: invented subjects make the brief untraceable and unsafe
dominance_rules.trigger: a factual field has no summary source
dominance_rules.action: block finalization until the field cites a summary fact or is marked stylistic

dominance_rules.rule: An audio brief naming a real person must carry an in-band consent reference, otherwise it defaults to non-impersonating description
dominance_rules.rationale: voice impersonation without consent is an identity and legal risk
dominance_rules.trigger: named-voice request without a consent reference
dominance_rules.action: force the non-impersonation default or require a populated consent reference

dominance_rules.rule: DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF must produce a self-contained artifact before HANDOFF_VALIDATION can certify it
dominance_rules.rationale: a brief that relies on shared state fails in a fresh session
dominance_rules.action: serialize the referenced context into the payload

dominance_rules.rule: PROMPT_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA must be fixed and versioned before any block is populated
dominance_rules.rationale: populating blocks against an unfixed schema causes rework when the shape changes
dominance_rules.trigger: block population begins without a pinned schema_version

dominance_rules.rule: DETERMINISM_PROVENANCE pointers must be current before emission so the brief is reproducible and auditable
dominance_rules.rationale: stale provenance misleads audit and breaks reproducibility
dominance_rules.trigger: a field edited without a provenance update
dominance_rules.action: rebuild provenance for the edited field before emission

dominance_rules.rule: HANDOFF_VALIDATION must run and pass before the artifact is emitted
dominance_rules.rationale: a malformed brief should fail here, not in the separate downstream session

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not assume the downstream session knows the contract; carry it in-band, or you will reissue every brief once an unlabeled output is discovered
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mass reissue of briefs after a dropped out-of-band contract causes unlabeled synthetic media

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not leave the disclosure slot optional; retrofitting a mandatory non-empty slot means revalidating every prior artifact
anti_rework_rules.prevents: bulk revalidation after unlabeled outputs surface

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not wire a render or publish path into this stage; removing it later requires re-architecting the pipeline boundary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pipeline re-architecture to restore scope containment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not invent prompt details ungrounded in the summary; auditing and removing them later is far costlier than grounding up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-hoc audit and rewrite of hallucinated prompt fields

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not reference this session's context in the handoff; making the artifact self-contained after the fact requires re-serialization of every brief
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-serialization of briefs that broke on a stateless boundary

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not populate blocks before pinning the schema version; a late schema change forces re-populating every block
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-population of all blocks after a schema reshape

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip provenance recording; reconstructing it for an audit means re-deriving every field from the summary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-derivation of field provenance during an audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not default audio to a named real voice; switching to a non-impersonation default later means revisiting every audio brief and its consent status
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rework of audio briefs to add consent or strip impersonation

iteration_protocol.trigger: an unlabeled synthetic output is found downstream
iteration_protocol.action: confirm the contract and disclosure tokens are embedded in IN_BAND_CONTRACT and that DISCLOSURE_SLOT is enforced non-empty

iteration_protocol.trigger: a downstream session fails for lack of carried context
iteration_protocol.action: make the DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF artifact fully self-contained and reject unresolved references in HANDOFF_VALIDATION

iteration_protocol.trigger: a render or publish path appears in this stage
iteration_protocol.action: remove it and re-assert the no-render boundary in SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS

iteration_protocol.trigger: an ungrounded invented detail is found in a brief
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the no-invention rule in GROUND_FROM_SUMMARY and require a provenance pointer in DETERMINISM_PROVENANCE

iteration_protocol.trigger: an impersonation request appears without consent
iteration_protocol.action: reinforce the non-impersonation default in AUDIO_BRIEF_SPEC and require an in-band consent reference in IN_BAND_CONTRACT

iteration_protocol.trigger: generations repeatedly violate a negative constraint
iteration_protocol.action: expand the negative-constraint list in IMAGE_PROMPT_SPEC and re-validate the image block

iteration_protocol.trigger: a brief that passed validation fails to parse downstream
iteration_protocol.action: pin HANDOFF_VALIDATION to the downstream parser contract and version PROMPT_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA with it

iteration_protocol.trigger: an audit cannot reproduce a brief from identical inputs
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild DETERMINISM_PROVENANCE pointers and confirm the deterministic build in GROUND_FROM_SUMMARY

priority_rationale: PROMPT_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA and GROUND_FROM_SUMMARY are foundational; IN_BAND_CONTRACT/DISCLOSURE_SLOT/SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS carry the safety scope finding; IMAGE/STORY/AUDIO specs populate the blocks; DOWNSTREAM_HANDOFF, DETERMINISM_PROVENANCE, and HANDOFF_VALIDATION close the emission.
